---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Extractive Materials Provision"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Extractive materials provision covers mineral extraction. The account values it from two World
Bank series, the share of a country's GDP that mineral rents represent and the GDP itself, with an
attribution factor applied to the resulting rent. The base year is 2019, and values are 2019 US
dollars at market exchange rates, the account's convention.

## Source

The write-up is `Extractive_Mineral_Provision.docx` in the shared folder of current write-ups,
and the authors' code is the `develop_yanxu` branch at `eff0d0b`. Both value mineral rents as a
share of GDP (the World Bank's CWoN 2024 rents for ten minerals) times GDP times a factor λ.

## Quantity

GDP in current USD, the World Bank series `NY.GDP.MKTP.CD`, read from the path recorded in
`es_config.csv` as `gep_quantity_input_path`. At the base year, current USD is 2019 USD. The
staged file is `API_NY.GDP.MKTP.CD_DS2_en_csv_v2_130122.csv`, dated 3 November 2025.

## Price

Mineral rents as a percentage of GDP, the World Bank series `NY.GDP.MINR.RT.ZS`, read from the
path recorded in `es_config.csv` as `gep_attribution_input_path`. The staged file is
`API_NY.GDP.MINR.RT.ZS_DS2_en_csv_v2_6559.csv`, dated 3 November 2025.

## Attribution

A factor of 0.49 is applied to the rent. `MINERAL_RENT_GEP_FACTOR` holds it in the tasks module.

## Valuation

`mineral_rent_gep` is the whole product:

$$
\text{GEP} = \frac{\text{mineral rent (\% of GDP)}}{100} \times \text{GDP (current USD)} \times 0.49
$$

The task reads each wide World Bank CSV and passes the frame to `world_bank_wide_to_long`, which
melts the year columns into long form keyed on `Country Code` and drops the descriptive columns
by not naming them. The two long tables are merged on `Country Code` and `year` and deduplicated
on that pair. `collapse_countries_to_r250` reduces the r264 correspondence to one canonical row
per country before the join, so a country that r264 splits is not repeated. The base-year table
is the rows where `year` equals `p.gep_base_year`. `utilities.sum_countries_to_year` sums the
value column by year for the time series.

Country references are published at 30 arcsecond simplification for this service, rather than the
300 arcsecond default the other modules use.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in
2019 USD. Of the 250, 88 carry a value, totalling \$99,544,328,382.62, 119 are computed zeros,
and 43 rows are missing, kept as missing rather than zero because an input carries no data for
those countries. A zero means the computation returned zero. A missing row means the data to
compute one is absent.

## Reproduction

The library equals the authors' own committed output of November 2025
(`outputs/extractive_materials_provision_gep.csv`) country for country, all 207 values and the
same total. That file labels Kosovo's row "Serbia".

The write-up reports \$198,741,283,557.50 in 2019 international dollars, which the authors'
current code computes from GDP in local currency divided by the PPP conversion factor. On World
Bank values fetched on 29 October 2026, that formula gives the write-up's total to the cent. The
difference from the library's total splits into two parts, and the 0.49 enters both sides
alike:

- GDP vintage, \$339,605,495.79. The fetched GDP revises 54 countries. The rent shares are
  unchanged.
- Currency basis, \$98,857,349,679.10. By country the international-dollar figure is a median
  2.50 times the US-dollar one, and nine countries without a PPP factor drop out.

## Inputs

Both data paths come from `es_config.csv` rather than `es_parameters.csv`. The
`extractive_materials_provision` row names `gep_quantity_input_path` for the GDP series and
`gep_attribution_input_path` for the mineral rent share. Its `gep_price_input_path` reads
`computed`, and its region columns are `n/a`, because the countries come from the account's own
correspondence. The service has no `es_parameters.csv` rows.

## Outputs

`gep_calculation` writes four tables into its own task directory:

- `gep_by_country_year_mineral.csv`, the merged long table with the valuation column.
- `gep_by_country_year.csv`, the same table carried forward.
- `gep_by_country_base_year.csv`, the 2019 rows, plus a matching `.gpkg` for mapping.
- `gep_by_year.csv` and an `.xlsx` alongside it, the annual totals.

The valuation column is `extractive_materials_provision_gep`, mirrored into a `Value` column for
the annual aggregation.

## Method constants

`MINERAL_RENT_GEP_FACTOR = 0.49`, applied to mineral rents times GDP in the valuation.

## Taken as given

Both World Bank series are used as published.

## What is open

The attribution factor has no stated source. The write-up writes GEP = λθ with no value for λ,
and neither the authors' code, the drive submission nor its `raw_data` notes gives a source for
0.49. The question is with the authors (open question 16). The factor stays as the authors set
it until they answer.

The write-up and the authors' code compute 2019 international dollars. The account reports 2019
US dollars at market exchange rates, as William's comment on the write-up states ("We are not
using international dollars (PPP), just the normal US$ 2019"). Bringing the write-up and code to
that convention is with the authors.

The staged GDP is the November 2025 download. Whether to refresh it to the current World Bank
vintage, worth \$339,605,495.79, is an account decision.

`gep_by_country_year.csv` and `gep_by_country_year_mineral.csv` are the same table written twice.
The valuation produces one row per country and year, so there is nothing for the second table to
add until the service gains a per-mineral breakdown.
